title: kernel prober: reservoir-based warmstart & time-sliced probing to reduce startup jitter for v3 kernels
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: We see intermittent P99 latency spikes during startup for long-context workloads after enabling FlashAttention v3 kernels in the general pool. Existing kernel prober logic (sequential probing across all candidate kernels on first requests) increases tail latency and memory churn on cold starts. Goal: Implement a reservoir-sampling-based kernel prober that performs time-sliced, bounded probes across a representative subset of kernels and shapes during warmstart. The prober should: - Limit additional overhead per request to <1% median latency and <5% P99 relative to baseline without probing - Use reservoir sampling of kernel candidates keyed by (model family, seq_len_bucket, dtype_quant) to keep probe set small and representative - Time-slice probes so no single request blocks waiting on probe evaluation; probes run asynchronously with a bounded concurrency budget - Cap memory / workspace allocations for probes to avoid destabilizing low-memory hosts - Respect routing policies: prefer same-arch kernel variants, and fallback to v2 or quantized kernels if v3 probes exceed loss/latency thresholds Success metrics: - Canary P50/P95/P99 delta vs baseline < 2% / 5% / 10% across test shapes - Regression detection: auto-disable v3 for a model-seq bucket if quality/latency breach is observed in 10 probes - Probe overhead budget met under synthetic workload runner (batch sizes 1..32, seq len 32..8192) Work to do: - Design: probe selector (reservoir sampler) and time-slice scheduler; probe result scoring (latency + token-quality delta) - Implementation: prober module in runtime, async probe worker pool, probe budget config - Observability: instrument probe counts, probe latency histogram, kernel-choice flips, probe-caused memory allocations - Safety: automatic rollback toggles, per-node probe rate-limiting, and canary policy for staged rollout - Tests: unit tests for sampler, integration tests with synthetic runner, end-to-end canary job in dedicated cluster Decisions & trade-offs: - Reservoir sampling biases toward recent successful kernels; we will seed reservoir with historical telemetry but allow decay to surface new kernels. This trades some exploration for stability. - Time-slicing probes (async) prioritizes request latency over immediate kernel discovery; it may delay optimal kernel selection by a few minutes but reduces startup jitter risk. - We will prefer to probe lightweight kernels first (quantized or small-block variants) to minimize memory churn, deferring large-v3 kernels unless budget allows. Links & artifacts: - Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUNTIME/pages/Kernel+Prober+Design - Design sketch (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/0B_prober_design_doc - Canary dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/runtime/kernel-prober-canary - Github implementation PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4219 Acceptance criteria: - New prober passes integration tests and canary run for three models (gpt-like 2B/6B/70B) with configured shapes - Prober configuration knobs surfaced in console for canary and global rollout - Rollback path validated (automatic disable on breach and manual toggle)

comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Patel: Created ticket after seeing two customer incidents where P99 spiked during startup for long-context retrieval workloads. Attached initial telemetry excerpts to Confluence.

2026-03-11 Luca Hernandez: PoC sampler implemented; validated reservoir correctness with synthetic list of kernels and shape keys. Observed correct replacement semantics and age-decay behavior. PR branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feature/kernel-prober-reservoir

2026-03-12 Grace Kim (SRE): Observability hooks reviewed. Requested probe memory accounting and a hard cap on probe workspace allocations; flagged low-memory node scenarios. Action: add node-level probe budget config.

2026-03-13 Research note: Quick experiment showed v3 gives 7% token-quality improvement for seq_len > 2048 but costs +12% P99 when probed synchronously. This motivates async time-slicing and preference for lightweight probes first.

2026-03-14 Luca Hernandez: Implemented time-slice scheduler and added probe-concurrency gauge. Running canary smoke tests; saw initial reduction in startup P99 spikes vs naive sequential prober. Filing PR for early review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4219 - reviewers: @mira, @oliver-s
2026-03-14 PM note (Evan Ortiz): Please add rollout checklist and customer impact communications for Dedicated customers who opt into early v3 adoption.
risks: Probe-caused memory spikes on low-memory nodes: mitigated by per-node budget and forced fallback to stable kernel
False positive regression detection: require multiple independent probe failures before disabling v3 for a bucket
Telemetry lag causing stale reservoir seeds: plan to seed from last 24h and decay older entries
rollback_plan: Feature flag off will immediately stop new probes and revert kernel selection to historical preference
Automated rollback: if canary P99 > baseline + 10% for 10m, disable v3 probes for affected bucket and notify on-call
Hotfix path: revert PR and redeploy runtime binary within 30m
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids probing all kernels at once; sampling reduces noise and operational cost.
Follow-on work may include integrating a simple bandit algorithm if reservoir sampling proves too conservative.
